source.text: וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֥ד שָׂטָ֖ן עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֨סֶת֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֔יד לִמְנ֖וֹת אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And stood up Satan against Israel, and incited David to count Israel.

en.L: And Satan stood up against Israel and incited David to count Israel.
en.B: Satan rose up against Israel and stirred David up to count Israel.
en.R: Satan came against Israel. He moved David to count the people of Israel.

es.L: Y se levantó Satanás contra Israel, e incitó a David a contar a Israel.
es.B: Satanás se levantó contra Israel e incitó a David a contar a Israel.
es.R: Satanás se puso en contra de Israel. Movió a David a contar a la gente de Israel.

fr.L: Et Satan se dressa contre Israël, et il incita David à dénombrer Israël.
fr.B: Satan se dressa contre Israël et poussa David à faire le dénombrement d’Israël.
fr.R: Satan s’est attaqué à Israël. Il a poussé David à compter les gens d’Israël.

sw.L: Shetani akasimama dhidi ya Israeli, akamchochea Daudi kuwahesabu Israeli.
sw.B: Shetani aliinuka dhidi ya Israeli, akamchochea Daudi kuwahesabu Israeli.
sw.R: Shetani alikuja dhidi ya Israeli. Akamshawishi Daudi kuwahesabu watu wa Israeli.

vi.L: Sa-tan nổi lên chống lại Y-sơ-ra-ên và xui giục Đa-vít kiểm tra dân số Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Sa-tan dấy lên chống lại Y-sơ-ra-ên và xúi giục Đa-vít kiểm tra dân số Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Sa-tan đến chống lại Y-sơ-ra-ên. Nó xúi Đa-vít đếm dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 사탄이 이스라엘을 대적하여 일어나서, 다윗을 부추겨 이스라엘을 세게 했다.
ko.B: 사탄이 이스라엘을 치려고 일어나서, 다윗을 부추겨 이스라엘의 인구를 세게 했다.
ko.R: 사탄이 이스라엘을 해치려고 나섰다. 사탄은 다윗의 마음을 움직여 이스라엘 백성을 세게 했다.

pt.L: E Satanás se levantou contra Israel e incitou Davi a contar Israel.
pt.B: Satanás se levantou contra Israel e instigou Davi a contar Israel.
pt.R: Satanás veio contra Israel. Ele levou Davi a contar o povo de Israel.

am.L: ሰይጣንም በእስራኤል ላይ ተነሣ፤ እስራኤልንም ይቆጥር ዘንድ ዳዊትን አነሣሣው።
am.B: ሰይጣን በእስራኤል ላይ ተነሥቶ እስራኤልን እንዲቆጥር ዳዊትን አነሣሣው።
am.R: ሰይጣን በእስራኤል ላይ መጣ። የእስራኤልን ሕዝብ እንዲቆጥር ዳዊትን ገፋፋው።

hi.L: और शैतान इस्राएल के विरुद्ध खड़ा हुआ, और उसने दाऊद को इस्राएल की गिनती करने के लिए उकसाया।
hi.B: शैतान इस्राएल के विरुद्ध उठ खड़ा हुआ और उसने दाऊद को इस्राएल की गिनती करने के लिए उभारा।
hi.R: शैतान इस्राएल के विरुद्ध आया। उसने दाऊद को इस्राएल के लोगों की गिनती करने के लिए उभारा।

ru.L: И восстал сатана против Израиля и побудил Давида исчислить Израиль.
ru.B: Сатана поднялся против Израиля и подтолкнул Давида пересчитать Израиль.
ru.R: Сатана выступил против Израиля. Он побудил Давида пересчитать народ Израиля.

ja.L: そしてサタンがイスラエルに対して立ち、ダビデをそそのかしてイスラエルを数えさせた。
ja.B: サタンがイスラエルに敵対して立ち上がり、ダビデをそそのかして、イスラエルを数えさせようとした。
ja.R: サタンがイスラエルに立ち向かってきました。サタンはダビデの心を動かして、イスラエルの人々を数えさせようとしました。

uk.L: І повстав сатана проти Ізраїля, і підбурив Давида перелічити Ізраїля.
uk.B: Сатана повстав проти Ізраїля й підбурив Давида перелічити Ізраїля.
uk.R: Сатана пішов проти Ізраїля. Він спонукав Давида перелічити ізраїльтян.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary who opposes God's people, here without the article and read as a name
alternatives: an adversary: an opponent, not named, who stood against Israel
the accuser of Job 1-2 and Zechariah 3, not yet used as a personal name
decisions.reason: The word means "adversary" or "accuser". In Job 1-2 and Zechariah 3:1-2 it has the article, "the adversary", a figure who stands in Yahweh's heavenly court and accuses. Here it has no article. That may mean it is used as a name, Satan, or that it means simply "an adversary", as it does of the human enemies Yahweh raised up against Solomon (1 Kings 11:14, 23, 25) and of the angel of Yahweh who stood in Balaam's way (Numbers 22:22). The verb "incited" is the one used of the adversary in Job 2:3. The text does not settle which is meant; this translation reads it as the name.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 21:1-27 retells 2 Samuel 24:1-25; here an adversary, not the anger of Yahweh, incites David
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:1 begins: "Again the anger of Yahweh burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, Go, count Israel and Judah." The Chronicler uses the same verb "incited" but names Satan as the one who stood against Israel. The two accounts look at one event from two sides: Scripture elsewhere speaks of God carrying out judgment through a hostile agent (1 Samuel 16:14; 1 Kings 22:19-23; see the note at 2 Samuel 24:1). This verse also leaves out "again" and has the plain "to count Israel" for David's spoken command. Each record of this chapter notes where its words differ from 2 Samuel 24.

decisions.choice: stood up against: took a stand as an opponent
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand or rise; with "against" it describes someone taking a position as an enemy. The adversary acts against Israel, and he does it by moving its king to sin.

decisions.choice: Satan
decisions.reason: Every level gives the word as a name, with a capital, since it has no article. The footnote gives "an adversary" as the other way to read it.

decisions.choice: stirred David up (Balanced); moved David (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:1. Readable also says "the people of Israel", as there.

decisions.choice: Satanás
decisions.reason: Read as a name, as the English does; the meaning decision gives the other reading, "an adversary".

decisions.choice: "Satan", as a name
decisions.reason: The word has no article here and is read as a name, as the meaning decision and the English do; French writes the usual "Satan".

decisions.choice: Shetani
decisions.reason: The English takes the word as the name Satan; Swahili has the established name "Shetani", used at every level. Where 2 Samuel 24:1 says Yahweh's anger incited David, Chronicles names Satan; the Swahili follows Chronicles.

decisions.choice: "Sa-tan"
decisions.reason: The English reads the word without the article as a name, so the Vietnamese uses the name of the New Testament and the style guide, "Sa-tan".

decisions.choice: "사탄" as a name at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no article, so the word is read as a name, as the English does; the meaning decision's other reading, "an adversary", stays in its footnote.

decisions.choice: Satanás, as a name, at every level
decisions.reason: For 1 Chronicles 21:1-27, which retells 2 Samuel 24 (m2), the Portuguese of 2 Samuel 24 is kept level by level where the Hebrew is the same, and only what Chronicles changes is changed. Here Chronicles names Satan where 2 Samuel 24:1 says that the anger of the LORD burned and "ele incitou Davi" (m2). Following the English and m1, the word without the article is read as a name and written "Satanás", the Portuguese name of the New Testament (docs/portuguese-style.md section 6), at every level; "um adversário" is the other reading, which m1 keeps in its footnote. The verb keeps 2 Samuel 24:1's words, "incitou" (L) and "instigou" (B); Readable "levou Davi a" as there.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in this chapter's Amharic (verses 3, 7, 8, 12, 13, 17, 26)
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic.

decisions.choice: "ሰይጣን" (Satan) as a name, the word of the Amharic New Testament; "አነሣሣው" (incited) kept from 2 Samuel 24:1
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word without the article as a name. 2 Samuel 24:1 has the anger of Yahweh inciting David; Chronicles has Satan, and the Amharic follows Chronicles' Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "शैतान" (Satan), as a name
decisions.reason: Where 2 Samuel 24:1 says that the anger of the LORD incited David, Chronicles names Satan (meanings m1, m2), so the wording differs. The word has no article and is read as a name, as the English does; "शैतान" is the New Testament's word in this translation. Read as a common noun it would be "an adversary".

decisions.choice: "उकसाया" (Literal); "उभारा" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb of 2 Samuel 24:1 keeps its Hindi at each level. This chapter retells 2 Samuel 24 and keeps its Hindi where the Hebrew is the same; where Chronicles differs, as here, so does the Hindi.

decisions.choice: "сатана" as the one who incites
decisions.reason: Chronicles retells 2 Samuel 24 (m2), but here an adversary, read as the name Satan (m1), incites David, where Samuel has the anger of the LORD; so the Russian differs from 2 Samuel 24:1 here. "Сатана" is written as in the New Testament in this translation. The verbs "побудил" (Literal, Readable) and "подтолкнул" (Balanced) and "исчислить" (Literal) are those of Samuel.

decisions.choice: satan "サタン" at every level, the name as in the New Testament Japanese.
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as a name; Japanese readers know サタン as the adversary.

decisions.choice: heset "そそのかす" (L, B), "心を動かす" (R); 2 Samuel 24:1 in Japanese has "動かして" with the LORD as subject.
decisions.reason: Here the adversary is the subject, so the verb of enticing fits.

decisions.choice: "сатана" written lower-case
decisions.reason: The common Ukrainian spelling, as in the Ukrainian Romans; the meaning decision reads the word as a name, which the lower-case form still carries.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד אֶל־יוֹאָב֙ וְאֶל־שָׂרֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם לְכ֗וּ סִפְרוּ֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבְּאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע וְעַד־דָּ֑ן וְהָבִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֔י וְאֵדְעָ֖ה אֶת־מִסְפָּרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Joab and to [the] commanders of the people, Go, count Israel from Beer-sheba and to Dan, and bring [it] to me, and I will know their number.

en.L: And David said to Joab and to the commanders of the people, "Go, count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring [the report] to me, so that I may know their number."
en.B: David told Joab and the troop commanders, "Go and count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, then bring me the report, so that I may know how many there are."
en.R: So David said to Joab and the army commanders, "Go and count the people of Israel, from Beersheba in the far south to Dan in the far north. Then bring me the report, so that I will know how many there are."

es.L: Y dijo David a Joab y a los jefes del pueblo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, {{plural_you:cuenten|contad}} a Israel desde Beerseba hasta Dan, y {{plural_you:tráiganme|traedme}} [el informe], para que yo sepa su número».
es.B: David les dijo a Joab y a los jefes de las tropas: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} el censo de Israel desde Beerseba hasta Dan, y luego {{plural_you:tráiganme|traedme}} el informe, para que yo sepa cuántos son».
es.R: Entonces David les dijo a Joab y a los jefes del ejército: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:cuenten|contad}} a la gente de Israel, desde Beerseba en el extremo sur hasta Dan en el extremo norte. Luego {{plural_you:tráiganme|traedme}} el informe, para que yo sepa cuántos son».

fr.L: Et David dit à Joab et aux chefs du peuple : « Allez, dénombrez Israël depuis Beer-Shéba jusqu’à Dan, et apportez-[moi le résultat], afin que je connaisse leur nombre. »
fr.B: David dit à Joab et aux chefs des troupes : « Allez faire le dénombrement d’Israël, depuis Beer-Shéba jusqu’à Dan, puis rapportez-moi le résultat, afin que je sache combien ils sont. »
fr.R: David a donc dit à Joab et aux chefs de l’armée : « Allez compter les gens d’Israël, depuis Beer-Shéba, tout au sud, jusqu’à Dan, tout au nord. Ensuite, rapportez-moi le résultat, pour que je sache combien ils sont. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Yoabu na wakuu wa watu, "Nendeni, mkawahesabu Israeli tangu Beer-sheba mpaka Dani, mniletee [habari], ili nijue idadi yao."
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia Yoabu na makamanda wa jeshi, "Nendeni mkawahesabu Israeli tangu Beer-sheba mpaka Dani, kisha mniletee habari, ili nijue wako wangapi."
sw.R: Basi Daudi akamwambia Yoabu na makamanda wa jeshi, "Nendeni mkawahesabu watu wa Israeli, tangu Beer-sheba kule kusini kabisa mpaka Dani kule kaskazini kabisa. Kisha mniletee habari, ili nijue wako wangapi."

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với Giô-áp và các tướng chỉ huy của dân: "Hãy đi kiểm tra dân số Y-sơ-ra-ên từ Bê-e-Sê-ba đến Đan, rồi đem [kết quả] về cho ta, để ta biết số dân."
vi.B: Đa-vít bảo Giô-áp và các tướng chỉ huy quân đội: "Hãy đi kiểm tra dân số Y-sơ-ra-ên từ Bê-e-Sê-ba đến Đan, rồi đem kết quả về cho ta, để ta biết họ có bao nhiêu người."
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít nói với Giô-áp và các tướng chỉ huy quân đội: "Hãy đi đếm dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, từ Bê-e-Sê-ba ở tận miền nam đến Đan ở tận miền bắc. Rồi đem kết quả về cho ta, để ta biết họ có bao nhiêu người."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 요압과 백성의 지휘관들에게 말했다. "가서 브엘세바에서 단까지 이스라엘을 세고 [그 결과를] 나에게 가져오너라. 그러면 내가 그들의 수를 알겠다."
ko.B: 다윗이 요압과 군대 지휘관들에게 말했다. "가서 브엘세바에서 단까지 이스라엘을 세고 그 결과를 나에게 보고하여라. 백성이 얼마나 되는지 알아야겠다."
ko.R: 그래서 다윗이 요압과 군대 지휘관들에게 말했다. "가서 남쪽 끝 브엘세바에서 북쪽 끝 단까지 이스라엘 백성을 세어라. 그리고 그 결과를 나에게 알려라. 그러면 백성이 얼마나 되는지 알 수 있을 것이다."

pt.L: E Davi disse a Joabe e aos comandantes do povo: "Vão, contem Israel desde Berseba até Dã, e tragam-me [o resultado], para que eu saiba o número deles."
pt.B: Davi disse a Joabe e aos comandantes das tropas: "Vão e contem Israel, de Berseba até Dã, e depois me tragam o resultado, para que eu saiba quantos são."
pt.R: Então Davi disse a Joabe e aos comandantes do exército: "Vão e contem o povo de Israel, desde Berseba, no extremo sul, até Dã, no extremo norte. Depois me tragam o resultado, para que eu saiba quantos são."

am.L: ዳዊትም ኢዮአብንና የሕዝቡን አለቆች፦ «ሂዱ፤ ከቤርሳቤህ እስከ ዳን ድረስ እስራኤልን ቁጠሩ፤ ቁጥራቸውንም አውቅ ዘንድ [ውጤቱን] አምጡልኝ» አላቸው።
am.B: ዳዊት ኢዮአብንና የሠራዊቱን አለቆች፦ «ሂዱና ከቤርሳቤህ እስከ ዳን ድረስ እስራኤልን ቁጠሩ፤ ምን ያህል እንደ ሆኑ አውቅ ዘንድ ውጤቱን አምጡልኝ» አላቸው።
am.R: ስለዚህ ዳዊት ኢዮአብንና የሠራዊቱን አለቆች እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «ሂዱና በደቡብ ዳርቻ ካለችው ከቤርሳቤህ አንሥቶ በሰሜን ዳርቻ እስካለችው እስከ ዳን ድረስ የእስራኤልን ሕዝብ ቁጠሩ። ከዚያም ምን ያህል እንደ ሆኑ እንዳውቅ ውጤቱን አምጡልኝ።»

hi.L: और दाऊद ने योआब से और लोगों के प्रधानों से कहा, "जाओ, बेर्शेबा से दान तक इस्राएल की गिनती करो, और [उसका लेखा] मेरे पास ले आओ, कि मैं उनकी गिनती जान लूँ।"
hi.B: दाऊद ने योआब और सेना के प्रधानों से कहा, "जाओ, बेर्शेबा से दान तक इस्राएल की गिनती करो, फिर मुझे उसका लेखा लाकर दो, ताकि मैं जान सकूँ कि वे कितने हैं।"
hi.R: तब दाऊद ने योआब और सेनापतियों से कहा, "जाओ और इस्राएल के लोगों की गिनती करो, दूर दक्षिण के बेर्शेबा से लेकर दूर उत्तर के दान तक। फिर मुझे उसका लेखा लाकर दो, ताकि मैं जान सकूँ कि वे कितने हैं।"

ru.L: И сказал Давид Иоаву и начальникам народа: «Пойдите, исчислите Израиль от Беэр-Шевы и до Дана, и принесите мне [донесение], чтобы я знал их число.»
ru.B: Давид сказал Иоаву и начальникам войска: «Пойдите и пересчитайте Израиль от Беэр-Шевы до Дана, а потом принесите мне донесение, чтобы я знал, сколько их.»
ru.R: И Давид сказал Иоаву и начальникам войска: «Пойдите и пересчитайте народ Израиля от Беэр-Шевы на крайнем юге до Дана на крайнем севере. Потом принесите мне донесение, чтобы я знал, сколько их.»

ja.L: そしてダビデはヨアブと民の長たちに言った。「行って、ベエル・シェバからダンまでイスラエルを数え、[その報告を]わたしのところに持って来なさい。わたしがその数を知るためである。」
ja.B: ダビデはヨアブと兵の指揮官たちに言った。「行って、ベエル・シェバからダンまでイスラエルを数え、その報告を持って来なさい。わたしはその数を知りたい。」
ja.R: そこでダビデは、ヨアブと軍の指揮官たちに言いました。「行って、南の果てのベエル・シェバから、北の果てのダンまで、イスラエルの人々を数えなさい。そして、その報告を持って来なさい。何人いるのか、知りたいのだ。」

uk.L: І сказав Давид Йоавові та начальникам народу: «Ідіть, перелічіть Ізраїля від Беер-Шеви й до Дану, і принесіть [звіт] мені, щоб я знав їхнє число.»
uk.B: Давид сказав Йоавові та начальникам війська: «Ідіть і перелічіть Ізраїля від Беер-Шеви до Дану, а тоді принесіть мені звіт, щоб я знав, скільки їх.»
uk.R: Тож Давид сказав Йоавові та начальникам війська: «Ідіть і перелічіть ізраїльтян, від Беер-Шеви на далекому півдні до Дану на далекій півночі. Тоді принесіть мені звіт, щоб я знав, скільки їх.»

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 24:2
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:2 has "the king" where this verse has "David", speaks to Joab alone as "the commander of the army who was with him", and tells him to "go about through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and register the people". Here the commanders are addressed together with Joab (in 2 Samuel 24:4 they go out with him), the verb is the ordinary word for counting, the land is named from south to north, and David adds "bring it to me".

decisions.choice: from Beersheba to Dan: the whole land, named from south to north
decisions.reason: Beersheba was the southernmost town of Israel and Dan the northernmost. 2 Samuel 24:2 names them from north to south; the Chronicler names them from south to north, as in 2 Chronicles 30:5. The sense is the same: the whole country.

decisions.choice: the commanders of the people: the officers of the army
decisions.reason: "The people" here means the people as an army, as often in Samuel and Chronicles (2 Samuel 18:1). These are the officers who carry out the count with Joab (2 Samuel 24:4).

decisions.choice: bring [the report] to me; bring me the report
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "bring to me", with no object. What is to be brought is the result of the count (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the troop commanders (Balanced); the army commanders; in the far south ... in the far north (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "troops" and "army" for "the people" as an army. Readable says where the two towns lay, as at 2 Samuel 24:2.

decisions.choice: "백성의 지휘관들" (L); "군대 지휘관들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's choice for "the people" meaning the army: the ordinary word at Literal, "군대" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: vocês (David to Joab and the commanders); contem; de Berseba até Dã
decisions.reason: David speaks to Joab and the commanders together, so every verb is plural ("Vão", "contem", "tragam"), the "vocês" of a king to his subjects. The plain verb "count" is "contar", as 2 Samuel 24:1 in Portuguese fixed it; the towns keep their Portuguese forms, named from south to north as Chronicles names them (m2), with Readable's "no extremo sul", "no extremo norte" from 2 Samuel 24:2.

decisions.choice: the king speaks to Joab and the commanders with "እናንተ" ("ሂዱ", "ቁጠሩ")
decisions.reason: A king speaks down to his officers, as David to Joab in 2 Samuel 24:2; Chronicles addresses the commanders too and names the land from Beersheba to Dan.

decisions.choice: "बेर्शेबा से दान तक"; "लोगों के प्रधानों" (Literal), "सेना के प्रधानों" (Balanced), "सेनापतियों" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Chronicles names the land from south to north (meaning m2), the reverse of 2 Samuel 24:2, and the Hindi keeps that order. "The commanders of the people" are army officers (m3); Literal keeps "people".

decisions.choice: "от Беэр-Шевы до Дана"
decisions.reason: Chronicles names the land from south to north, the reverse of 2 Samuel 24:2 (m1, m2), and speaks to Joab and the commanders together.

decisions.choice: sarei ha'am "民の長たち" (L), "兵の指揮官たち" (B), "軍の指揮官たち" (R); the king to Joab in plain speech.
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the officers of the army; ha'am as army follows the 2SA forms (民 L, 兵 B).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב יוֹסֵף֩ יְהוָ֨ה עַל־עַמּ֤וֹ׀כָּהֵם֙ מֵאָ֣ה פְעָמִ֔ים הֲלֹא֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֻּלָּ֥ם לַאדֹנִ֖י לַעֲבָדִ֑ים לָ֣מָּה יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ זֹאת֙ אֲדֹנִ֔י לָ֛מָּה יִהְיֶ֥ה לְאַשְׁמָ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joab, May add Yahweh to his people as they [are] a hundred times; [are they] not, my lord the king, all of them to my lord as servants? Why does seek this my lord? Why should it be as guilt for Israel?

en.L: And Joab said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} add to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people a hundred times as many as they [are]! My lord the king, are they not all my lord's servants? Why does my lord seek this? Why should it become [a cause of] guilt for Israel?"
en.B: But Joab said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people a hundred times as many as they are! Are they not all, my lord the king, servants of my lord? Why does my lord wish for this? Why should it be a cause of guilt for Israel?"
en.R: But Joab answered, "I pray that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people a hundred times more than they are now! My king, all of them are already your subjects. Why do you want to do this? Why should you bring guilt on Israel?"

es.L: Y dijo Joab: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} añada a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo cien veces más de lo que son! Mi señor el rey, ¿no son todos ellos siervos de mi señor? ¿Por qué busca esto mi señor? ¿Por qué ha de ser [causa de] culpa para Israel?».
es.B: Pero Joab dijo: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo cien veces más numeroso de lo que es! ¿No son todos ellos, mi señor el rey, siervos de mi señor? ¿Por qué quiere mi señor hacer esto? ¿Por qué ha de ser causa de culpa para Israel?».
es.R: Pero Joab respondió: «¡Le pido a {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que haga a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo cien veces más numeroso de lo que es ahora! Mi rey, todos ellos ya son tus súbditos. ¿Por qué quieres hacer esto? ¿Por qué has de traer culpa sobre Israel?».

fr.L: Et Joab dit : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ajoute à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple cent fois autant qu’ils sont ! Mon seigneur le roi, ne sont-ils pas tous les serviteurs de mon seigneur ? Pourquoi mon seigneur recherche-t-il cela ? Pourquoi cela deviendrait-il [une cause de] culpabilité pour Israël ? »
fr.B: Mais Joab dit : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} rende {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple cent fois plus nombreux qu’il ne l’est ! Mon seigneur le roi, ne sont-ils pas tous les serviteurs de mon seigneur ? Pourquoi mon seigneur veut-il cela ? Pourquoi rendre Israël coupable ? »
fr.R: Mais Joab a répondu : « Je prie pour que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} rende {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple cent fois plus nombreux qu’il ne l’est maintenant ! Mon roi, tous ces gens sont déjà tes sujets. Pourquoi veux-tu faire cela ? Pourquoi veux-tu rendre Israël coupable ? »

sw.L: Yoabu akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na awaongeze watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mara mia kama walivyo! Bwana wangu mfalme, je, wote si watumishi wa bwana wangu? Kwa nini bwana wangu anatafuta jambo hili? Kwa nini liwe [sababu ya] hatia kwa Israeli?"
sw.B: Lakini Yoabu akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na awazidishe watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mara mia kuliko walivyo! Bwana wangu mfalme, je, wote si watumishi wa bwana wangu? Kwa nini bwana wangu anataka jambo hili? Kwa nini liwe sababu ya hatia kwa Israeli?"
sw.R: Lakini Yoabu akajibu, "Naomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awafanye watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kuwa wengi mara mia kuliko walivyo sasa! Mfalme wangu, wote tayari ni raia wako. Kwa nini unataka kufanya jambo hili? Kwa nini uwaletee Israeli hatia?"

vi.L: Giô-áp nói: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thêm dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên gấp trăm lần như hiện nay! Thưa chúa tôi là vua, chẳng phải tất cả họ đều là đầy tớ của chúa tôi sao? Sao chúa tôi lại tìm việc này? Sao để nó trở thành [cớ] mắc tội cho Y-sơ-ra-ên?"
vi.B: Nhưng Giô-áp thưa: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm cho dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đông gấp trăm lần hiện nay! Tâu bệ hạ, chẳng phải tất cả họ đều là đầy tớ của bệ hạ sao? Sao bệ hạ lại muốn việc này? Sao lại để nó thành cớ mắc tội cho Y-sơ-ra-ên?"
vi.R: Nhưng Giô-áp trả lời: "Tôi cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm cho dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đông gấp trăm lần hiện nay! Thưa đức vua, tất cả họ đã là thần dân của đức vua rồi. Sao đức vua lại muốn làm việc này? Sao đức vua lại đem tội lỗi đến cho Y-sơ-ra-ên?"

ko.L: 그리고 요압이 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 백성을 지금보다 백 배나 더하시기를 바랍니다! 내 주 임금님, 그들은 모두 내 주의 종들이 아닙니까? 어찌하여 내 주께서 이 일을 원하십니까? 어찌하여 이것이 이스라엘에게 죄가 되게 하려 하십니까?"
ko.B: 그러나 요압이 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 백성을 지금보다 백 배나 많게 하시기를 바랍니다! 내 주 임금님, 그들은 모두 내 주의 종들이 아닙니까? 그런데 내 주께서는 왜 이 일을 하려고 하십니까? 왜 이스라엘에게 죄를 지우려 하십니까?"
ko.R: 그러나 요압이 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 백성을 지금보다 백 배나 많게 하시기를 빕니다! 임금님, 그들은 이미 모두 임금님의 백성입니다. 그런데 왜 이 일을 하려고 하십니까? 왜 이스라엘에게 죄를 지게 하십니까?"

pt.L: E Joabe disse: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} acrescente ao {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo cem vezes tantos quantos eles [são]! Ó meu senhor, o rei, não são todos eles servos do meu senhor? Por que o meu senhor busca isto? Por que haveria de ser [motivo de] culpa para Israel?"
pt.B: Mas Joabe disse: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} multiplique o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo cem vezes mais do que ele é! Meu senhor, o rei, não são todos eles servos do meu senhor? Por que o meu senhor quer isso? Por que isso haveria de trazer culpa sobre Israel?"
pt.R: Mas Joabe respondeu: "Peço que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} faça o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo cem vezes maior do que é agora! Meu rei, todos eles já são súditos do senhor. Por que o senhor quer fazer isso? Por que o senhor vai trazer culpa sobre Israel?"

am.L: ኢዮአብም እንዲህ አለ፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በሕዝቡ ላይ እንዳሉት መቶ እጥፍ ይጨምር! ጌታዬ ንጉሥ ሆይ፣ ሁሉም የጌታዬ ባሪያዎች አይደሉምን? ጌታዬ ይህን ለምን ይሻል? ለእስራኤልስ ለምን የበደል [ምክንያት] ይሆናል?»
am.B: ኢዮአብ ግን እንዲህ አለ፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕዝቡን አሁን ካሉት መቶ እጥፍ ያብዛው! ጌታዬ ንጉሥ ሆይ፣ ሁሉም የጌታዬ አገልጋዮች አይደሉምን? ጌታዬ ይህን ለምን ፈለገ? ለእስራኤልስ ለምን የበደል ምክንያት ይሆናል?»
am.R: ኢዮአብ ግን እንዲህ ሲል መለሰ፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕዝቡን አሁን ካሉት መቶ እጥፍ እንዲያበዛ እጸልያለሁ! ንጉሥ ሆይ፣ እነዚህ ሁሉ አስቀድመው የእርስዎ ተገዢዎች ናቸው። ይህን ማድረግ ለምን ፈለጉ? በእስራኤልስ ላይ ለምን በደል ያመጣሉ?»

hi.L: और योआब ने कहा, "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} अपनी प्रजा को, जितने वे [हैं], सौ गुना बढ़ाएँ! हे मेरे स्वामी राजा, क्या वे सब मेरे स्वामी के दास नहीं हैं? मेरे स्वामी यह क्यों चाहते हैं? यह इस्राएल के लिए दोष का [कारण] क्यों बने?"
hi.B: पर योआब ने कहा, "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} अपनी प्रजा को अभी से सौ गुना अधिक कर दें! हे मेरे स्वामी राजा, क्या वे सब मेरे स्वामी के दास नहीं हैं? मेरे स्वामी ऐसा क्यों चाहते हैं? यह इस्राएल पर दोष का कारण क्यों बने?"
hi.R: पर योआब ने उत्तर दिया, "मेरी प्रार्थना है कि {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} अपनी प्रजा को अभी से सौ गुना बढ़ा दें! महाराज, ये सब तो पहले से ही आपकी प्रजा हैं। आप ऐसा क्यों करना चाहते हैं? आप इस्राएल पर दोष क्यों लाना चाहते हैं?"

ru.L: И сказал Иоав: «Пусть прибавит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} к своему народу во сто крат против того, сколько их есть! Господин мой царь, разве не все они рабы господина моего? Зачем этого ищет господин мой? Зачем быть [этому] виной для Израиля?»
ru.B: Но Иоав сказал: «Пусть {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} умножит свой народ во сто раз против того, что есть! Разве не все они, господин мой царь, рабы господина моего? Зачем господину моему этого хотеть? Зачем навлекать вину на Израиль?»
ru.R: Но Иоав ответил: «Пусть {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} сделает свой народ в сто раз больше, чем теперь! Мой царь, все они и так твои подданные. Зачем тебе это нужно? Зачем навлекать вину на Израиль?»

ja.L: しかしヨアブは言った。「{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が、ご自分の民を今の百倍に増し加えてくださいますように。わたしの主君、王よ、彼らはみな、わたしの主君のしもべではありませんか？なぜ、わたしの主君はこのことを求められるのですか？なぜ、それがイスラエルにとって罪過[の原因]となるのですか？」
ja.B: しかしヨアブは言った。「{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が、ご自分の民を今の百倍にも増やしてくださいますように。わが主君、王さま、彼らはみな、わが主君のしもべではありませんか？なぜ、わが主君はこのようなことを望まれるのですか？なぜ、それがイスラエルに罪をもたらすことになってよいのでしょうか？」
ja.R: しかしヨアブは答えました。「{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が、ご自分の民を今の百倍にも増やしてくださいますように。王さま、この人々はみな、もう王さまの民です。なぜ、こんなことをなさりたいのですか？なぜ、イスラエルに罪を負わせるようなことをなさるのですか？」

uk.L: І сказав Йоав: «Нехай {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} додасть до свого народу в сто разів більше, ніж їх [є]! Мій пане царю, хіба не всі вони раби мого пана? Навіщо мій пан шукає цього? Навіщо це має стати провиною для Ізраїля?»
uk.B: Але Йоав сказав: «Нехай {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} зробить свій народ у сто разів численнішим, ніж він є! Хіба ж вони, мій пане царю, не всі раби мого пана? Навіщо мій пан цього бажає? Навіщо накликати провину на Ізраїля?»
uk.R: Але Йоав відповів: «Нехай {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} зробить свій народ у сто разів численнішим, ніж тепер! Мій царю, усі вони й так твої піддані. Навіщо тобі це робити? Навіщо тобі накликати провину на Ізраїля?»

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 24:3
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:3 has "Yahweh your God", "the people", the doubled "as they are and as they are", and the wish "while the eyes of my lord the king see it"; it asks why the king "delights in" this thing. Here Joab says "his people", adds the question "are they not all my lord's servants?", uses the verb "seek", and ends with a second question that 2 Samuel does not have: why should this bring guilt on Israel?

decisions.choice: guilt: guilt that makes the people liable to punishment
decisions.reason: The word names a wrong together with the liability it brings, as when a priest's sin brings guilt on the people (Leviticus 4:3). Joab sees that the king's census will make all Israel answerable for it, and so it does (verse 7).

decisions.choice: are they not all my lord's servants?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: Joab's point is that the people already belong to the king. Counting them adds nothing to what he has; only Yahweh can increase them.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: The word, which can mean "slave", here names the king's subjects, as it names a king's officials elsewhere; the whole people are his to command. Literal and Balanced say "servants", as for the king's officials; Readable says "subjects".

decisions.choice: My king, all of them are already your subjects; Why should you bring guilt on Israel?
decisions.reason: Joab speaks of the king in the third person, as a courtier did. Readable lets him speak to David directly, turns the first question into the statement it implies, and says "subjects" for the king's people.

decisions.choice: Mi rey; tú (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns Joab's third-person "my lord" into direct address with "tú", as the English does; Literal and Balanced keep "mi señor el rey", as in Samuel.

decisions.choice: "chúa tôi là vua" (L), "bệ hạ" (B), "đức vua" (R)
decisions.reason: The Kings terms note's address forms for a subject speaking to the king, used for Joab, Gad and Ornan in this chapter.

decisions.choice: Joab speaks to the king in 합쇼체 with "내 주 임금님" and "내 주" (L, B), "임금님" (R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's address to the king; Readable lets Joab speak to David directly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: o meu senhor, o rei (L, B); o senhor, meu rei (R); servos (L, B), súditos (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 24:3 in Portuguese: Joab speaks of the king in the courtly third person, "o meu senhor", and Readable lets him speak to David directly with "o senhor", as the English Readable says "you". The wish "cem vezes" keeps 2 Samuel's words; the rest is Chronicles' own (m1): "o seu povo", the LORD's people, and the questions about the king's servants and Israel's guilt (m2).

decisions.choice: Joab speaks to David as "ጌታዬ ንጉሥ" in the courtly third person (L, B) and with "እርስዎ" at Readable ("የእርስዎ", "ፈለጉ", "ያመጣሉ")
decisions.reason: A commander addresses his king with the respectful forms, as in 2 Samuel 24:3. Chronicles has "his people" for "your God ... the people", and its own questions about servants and guilt, which the Amharic follows.

decisions.choice: "मेरे स्वामी राजा" with honorific verbs ("चाहते हैं"); "महाराज" and "आप" (Readable); "दास" (Literal, Balanced), "प्रजा" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Joab speaks to the king in the courtly third person, as in 2 Samuel 24:3; Readable lets him speak to David directly with "महाराज", as the English Readable does. The king's "servants" here are his subjects (m3): Readable says "प्रजा". The king says "तुम" to Joab.

decisions.choice: "свой народ", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: With the LORD as subject Russian uses the reflexive "свой", which takes no span; the English has one on "his".

decisions.choice: Joab to David in です・ます; adoni hammelekh "わたしの主君、王よ" (L), "わが主君、王さま" (B), "王さま" (R); "servants" "しもべ" (L, B), "王さまの民" (R, as the English "subjects").
decisions.reason: The court address settled for 1-2 Samuel and 1 Kings.

decisions.choice: ashmah "罪過" (L), "罪" (B, R).
decisions.reason: Guilt that makes the people liable to punishment, said plainly at B and R.

source.text: וּדְבַר־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָזַ֣ק עַל־יוֹאָ֑ב וַיֵּצֵ֣א יוֹאָ֗ב וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ֙ בְּכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] word of the king prevailed against Joab; and went out Joab and went about through all Israel, and came [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: But the king's word prevailed against Joab. So Joab went out and went about through all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.
en.B: But the king's order overruled Joab, so Joab went out and traveled through all Israel, and then came back to Jerusalem.
en.R: But the king would not change his order, even though Joab was against it. So Joab left and went all through Israel. Then he came back to Jerusalem.

es.L: Pero la palabra del rey prevaleció sobre Joab. Y salió Joab y recorrió todo Israel, y volvió a Jerusalén.
es.B: Pero la orden del rey se impuso a Joab, así que Joab salió y recorrió todo Israel, y luego volvió a Jerusalén.
es.R: Pero el rey no quiso cambiar su orden, aunque Joab estaba en contra. Así que Joab salió y recorrió todo Israel. Después volvió a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Mais la parole du roi l’emporta sur Joab. Et Joab sortit, et parcourut tout Israël, et arriva [à] Jérusalem.
fr.B: Mais l’ordre du roi s’imposa à Joab. Joab partit donc, parcourut tout Israël, puis revint à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Mais le roi n’a pas voulu changer son ordre, même si Joab n’était pas d’accord. Joab est donc parti, et il a parcouru tout Israël. Ensuite, il est revenu à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Lakini neno la mfalme likamshinda Yoabu. Basi Yoabu akatoka akazunguka katika Israeli yote, akafika Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Lakini amri ya mfalme ikashinda maoni ya Yoabu, kwa hiyo Yoabu akaondoka akapita katika Israeli yote, kisha akarudi Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Lakini mfalme hakubadili amri yake, ingawa Yoabu aliipinga. Kwa hiyo Yoabu akaondoka, akapita katika Israeli yote. Kisha akarudi Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Nhưng lời vua thắng Giô-áp. Vậy Giô-áp ra đi, đi khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên, rồi trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Nhưng lệnh của vua đã gạt bỏ ý kiến của Giô-áp, nên Giô-áp ra đi, đi khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên rồi trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Nhưng vua không chịu đổi lệnh, dù Giô-áp phản đối. Vậy Giô-áp ra đi và đi khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên. Rồi ông trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그러나 왕의 말이 요압을 이겼다. 그래서 요압이 나가서 온 이스라엘을 두루 다니고 예루살렘에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 그러나 요압은 왕의 명령을 꺾지 못했다. 그래서 요압은 나가서 온 이스라엘을 두루 다닌 뒤 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.
ko.R: 그러나 요압이 반대했는데도 왕은 명령을 바꾸지 않았다. 그래서 요압은 떠나서 이스라엘 곳곳을 다녔다. 그리고 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.

pt.L: Mas a palavra do rei prevaleceu sobre Joabe. E Joabe saiu e percorreu todo o Israel, e veio a Jerusalém.
pt.B: Mas a ordem do rei se impôs a Joabe. Então Joabe saiu, percorreu todo o Israel e depois voltou a Jerusalém.
pt.R: Mas o rei não quis mudar a sua ordem, mesmo com Joabe contra ela. Então Joabe saiu e foi por todo o Israel. Depois voltou para Jerusalém.

am.L: ነገር ግን የንጉሡ ቃል በኢዮአብ ላይ በረታ። ስለዚህ ኢዮአብ ወጥቶ በእስራኤል ሁሉ ተዘዋወረ፤ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምም መጣ።
am.B: ነገር ግን የንጉሡ ትእዛዝ በኢዮአብ ላይ አየለ፤ ስለዚህ ኢዮአብ ወጥቶ በእስራኤል ሁሉ ተጓዘ፤ ከዚያም ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሰ።
am.R: ኢዮአብ ቢቃወምም ንጉሡ ትእዛዙን አልለወጠም። ስለዚህ ኢዮአብ ወጥቶ በእስራኤል ሁሉ ዞረ። ከዚያም ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሰ።

hi.L: पर राजा की बात योआब पर प्रबल हुई। इसलिए योआब निकलकर सारे इस्राएल में घूमा, और यरूशलेम आया।
hi.B: पर राजा का आदेश योआब की बात पर भारी पड़ा, इसलिए योआब निकलकर सारे इस्राएल में घूमा, और फिर यरूशलेम लौट आया।
hi.R: योआब इसके विरुद्ध था, फिर भी राजा ने अपना आदेश नहीं बदला। इसलिए योआब निकलकर पूरे इस्राएल में घूमा। फिर वह यरूशलेम लौट आया।

ru.L: Но слово царя возобладало над Иоавом. И вышел Иоав, и прошёл по всему Израилю, и пришёл в Иерусалим.
ru.B: Но приказ царя взял верх над Иоавом, и Иоав вышел, прошёл по всему Израилю и вернулся в Иерусалим.
ru.R: Но царь не стал менять своего приказа, хотя Иоав был против. И Иоав ушёл и прошёл по всему Израилю. Потом он вернулся в Иерусалим.

ja.L: しかし王の言葉はヨアブに勝った。そこでヨアブは出て行き、全イスラエルを巡り歩いて、エルサレムに来た。
ja.B: しかし王の命令はヨアブを押し切った。そこでヨアブは出て行って、イスラエル全土を巡り、エルサレムに帰って来た。
ja.R: けれども、ヨアブが反対しても、王は命令を変えませんでした。そこでヨアブは出かけて行き、イスラエル中を回りました。それから、エルサレムに戻って来ました。

uk.L: Але слово царя переважило Йоава. І вийшов Йоав, і обійшов увесь Ізраїль, і прийшов до Єрусалиму.
uk.B: Але царський наказ переважив Йоава, тож Йоав вийшов, обійшов увесь Ізраїль і повернувся до Єрусалиму.
uk.R: Але цар не скасував свого наказу, хоч Йоав був проти. Тож Йоав вирушив і обійшов увесь Ізраїль. Потім він повернувся до Єрусалиму.

decisions.choice: a short form of 2 Samuel 24:4-8
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:4 says the king's word prevailed "against Joab and against the commanders of the army", and 24:5-8 traces their route around the land, from Aroer east of the Jordan north to Dan and Sidon, then south to Beersheba, ending in Jerusalem "at the end of nine months and twenty days". The Chronicler names only Joab and gives the whole journey in one line.

decisions.choice: the king's word prevailed against Joab: the king overruled him
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:4. The verb means "was strong against": the king's command won over Joab's objection.

decisions.choice: came back
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:8. Joab set out from Jerusalem, so Balanced and Readable say he came back.

decisions.choice: would not change his order, even though Joab was against it
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:4: Readable spells out what "prevailed against" implies.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 24:4, shortened
decisions.reason: The opening keeps 2 Samuel 24:4 in Portuguese ("prevaleceu sobre" / "se impôs a" / "não quis mudar a sua ordem"), without the commanders of the army, and the route of 2 Samuel 24:5-8 is summed up as Chronicles sums it up (m1), with "voltou" at Balanced and Readable, as 2 Samuel 24:8.

decisions.choice: the first clause as 2 Samuel 24:4 ("በረታ" L, "አየለ" B, R "ትእዛዙን አልለወጠም"), without the army commanders
decisions.reason: Chronicles names Joab alone and sums up the journey of 2 Samuel 24:4-8 in one clause.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־מִסְפַּ֥ר מִפְקַד־הָעָ֖ם אֶל־דָּוִ֑יד וַיְהִ֣י כָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל אֶ֣לֶף אֲלָפִים֩ וּמֵאָ֨ה אֶ֤לֶף אִישׁ֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב וִֽיהוּדָ֕ה אַרְבַּע֩ מֵא֨וֹת וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Joab [the] number of the registration of the people to David; and was all Israel a thousand thousands and a hundred thousand men drawing [the] sword, and Judah four hundred and seventy thousand men drawing [the] sword.

en.L: And Joab gave the number of the registration of the people to David. And all Israel was 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, and Judah [was] 470,000 men who drew the sword.
en.B: Joab gave David the total of the people who had been registered: in all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who could handle a sword, and in Judah 470,000 men who could handle a sword.
en.R: Joab gave David the results of the count. In all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who could fight with a sword. In Judah there were 470,000 men who could fight with a sword.

es.L: Y Joab dio a David el número del censo del pueblo. Y todo Israel era 1 100 000 hombres que sacaban espada, y Judá 470 000 hombres que sacaban espada.
es.B: Joab le dio a David el total de la gente censada: en todo Israel había 1 100 000 hombres que sabían manejar la espada, y en Judá 470 000 hombres que sabían manejar la espada.
es.R: Joab le dio a David el resultado del censo. En todo Israel había 1 100 000 hombres que podían pelear con espada. En Judá había 470 000 hombres que podían pelear con espada.

fr.L: Et Joab donna à David le chiffre du recensement du peuple. Et tout Israël était de 1 100 000 hommes tirant l’épée, et Juda, de 470 000 hommes tirant l’épée.
fr.B: Joab remit à David le chiffre du recensement du peuple : il y avait dans tout Israël 1 100 000 hommes capables de manier l’épée, et en Juda 470 000 hommes capables de manier l’épée.
fr.R: Joab a donné à David les résultats du recensement. Dans tout Israël, il y avait 1 100 000 hommes capables de se battre avec une épée. En Juda, il y avait 470 000 hommes capables de se battre avec une épée.

sw.L: Yoabu akampa Daudi hesabu ya kuandikishwa kwa watu. Na Israeli wote walikuwa watu 1,100,000 waliochomoa upanga, na Yuda [walikuwa] watu 470,000 waliochomoa upanga.
sw.B: Yoabu akampa Daudi jumla ya watu walioandikishwa: katika Israeli wote walikuwa wanaume 1,100,000 walioweza kutumia upanga, na katika Yuda wanaume 470,000 walioweza kutumia upanga.
sw.R: Yoabu akampa Daudi matokeo ya hesabu. Katika Israeli wote walikuwa wanaume 1,100,000 walioweza kupigana kwa upanga. Katika Yuda walikuwa wanaume 470,000 walioweza kupigana kwa upanga.

vi.L: Giô-áp trao cho Đa-vít con số kiểm tra dân số. Cả Y-sơ-ra-ên có 1.100.000 người cầm gươm, và Giu-đa [có] 470.000 người cầm gươm.
vi.B: Giô-áp trình lên Đa-vít tổng số dân đã được kiểm tra: trong cả Y-sơ-ra-ên có 1.100.000 người có thể cầm gươm, và trong Giu-đa có 470.000 người có thể cầm gươm.
vi.R: Giô-áp báo cho Đa-vít kết quả cuộc kiểm tra dân số. Trong cả Y-sơ-ra-ên có 1.100.000 người có thể cầm gươm chiến đấu. Trong Giu-đa có 470.000 người có thể cầm gươm chiến đấu.

ko.L: 그리고 요압이 등록한 백성의 수를 다윗에게 보고했다. 온 이스라엘은 칼을 빼는 사람이 110만 명이었고, 유다는 칼을 빼는 사람이 47만 명이었다.
ko.B: 요압은 등록된 백성의 총수를 다윗에게 보고했다. 온 이스라엘에는 칼을 다룰 줄 아는 남자가 110만 명, 유다에는 칼을 다룰 줄 아는 남자가 47만 명이 있었다.
ko.R: 요압은 백성을 센 결과를 다윗에게 알렸다. 온 이스라엘에는 칼을 들고 싸울 수 있는 남자가 110만 명이 있었다. 유다에는 칼을 들고 싸울 수 있는 남자가 47만 명이 있었다.

pt.L: E Joabe deu a Davi o número do recenseamento do povo. E todo o Israel era um milhão e cem mil homens que empunhavam a espada, e Judá, quatrocentos e setenta mil homens que empunhavam a espada.
pt.B: Joabe entregou a Davi o total dos recenseados: em todo o Israel havia um milhão e cem mil homens que sabiam manejar a espada, e em Judá, quatrocentos e setenta mil homens que sabiam manejar a espada.
pt.R: Joabe deu a Davi o resultado da contagem. Em todo o Israel havia um milhão e cem mil homens que podiam lutar com a espada. Em Judá havia quatrocentos e setenta mil homens que podiam lutar com a espada.

am.L: ኢዮአብም የሕዝቡን የምዝገባ ቁጥር ለዳዊት ሰጠ፤ እስራኤልም ሁሉ ሰይፍ የሚመዝዙ 1,100,000 ሰዎች ነበሩ፤ ይሁዳም ሰይፍ የሚመዝዙ 470,000 ሰዎች [ነበሩ]።
am.B: ኢዮአብ የተመዘገቡትን ሰዎች ጠቅላላ ቁጥር ለዳዊት ሰጠ፤ በእስራኤል ሁሉ ሰይፍ መምዘዝ የሚችሉ 1,100,000 ሰዎች፣ በይሁዳም ሰይፍ መምዘዝ የሚችሉ 470,000 ሰዎች ነበሩ።
am.R: ኢዮአብ የቆጠራውን ውጤት ለዳዊት ሰጠ። በእስራኤል ሁሉ በሰይፍ መዋጋት የሚችሉ 1,100,000 ሰዎች ነበሩ። በይሁዳ ደግሞ በሰይፍ መዋጋት የሚችሉ 470,000 ሰዎች ነበሩ።

hi.L: और योआब ने लोगों की नाम-लिखाई की गिनती दाऊद को दी। और सारे इस्राएल में तलवार चलानेवाले 11,00,000 पुरुष [थे], और यहूदा में तलवार चलानेवाले 4,70,000 पुरुष [थे]।
hi.B: योआब ने दाऊद को नाम लिखे गए लोगों की कुल गिनती बताई: सारे इस्राएल में 11,00,000 पुरुष थे जो तलवार चला सकते थे, और यहूदा में 4,70,000 पुरुष जो तलवार चला सकते थे।
hi.R: योआब ने दाऊद को गिनती का परिणाम बताया। सारे इस्राएल में 11,00,000 पुरुष थे जो तलवार से लड़ सकते थे। यहूदा में 4,70,000 पुरुष थे जो तलवार से लड़ सकते थे।

ru.L: И дал Иоав Давиду число переписанного народа; и был весь Израиль — 1 100 000 мужей, обнажающих меч, а Иуда — 470 000 мужей, обнажающих меч.
ru.B: Иоав сообщил Давиду, сколько людей было переписано: во всём Израиле было 1 100 000 мужчин, способных владеть мечом, а в Иуде — 470 000 мужчин, способных владеть мечом.
ru.R: Иоав сообщил Давиду, что показал подсчёт. Во всём Израиле было 1 100 000 мужчин, которые могли сражаться мечом. В Иуде было 470 000 мужчин, которые могли сражаться мечом.

ja.L: そしてヨアブは民の登録の数をダビデに渡した。全イスラエルは剣を抜く男が百十万人、ユダは剣を抜く男が四十七万人であった。
ja.B: ヨアブは、登録された民の総数をダビデに報告した。全イスラエルには剣を使うことのできる男が百十万人、ユダには剣を使うことのできる男が四十七万人いた。
ja.R: ヨアブは、数えた結果をダビデに報告しました。イスラエル全体には、剣で戦うことのできる男が百十万人いました。ユダには、剣で戦うことのできる男が四十七万人いました。

uk.L: І дав Йоав Давидові число перепису народу. І ввесь Ізраїль був тисяча тисяч і сто тисяч чоловіків, що витягають меч, а Юда — чотириста сімдесят тисяч чоловіків, що витягають меч.
uk.B: Йоав подав Давидові загальне число переписаного народу: в усьому Ізраїлі було мільйон сто тисяч чоловіків, здатних носити меч, а в Юді — чотириста сімдесят тисяч чоловіків, здатних носити меч.
uk.R: Йоав подав Давидові підсумки перепису. В усьому Ізраїлі було мільйон сто тисяч чоловіків, які могли битися мечем. У Юді було чотириста сімдесят тисяч чоловіків, які могли битися мечем.

decisions.choice: 1,100,000 in all Israel and 470,000 in Judah: the figures of this account
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:9, telling the same story, gives 800,000 for Israel and 500,000 for Judah. 1 Chronicles 27:24 says that Joab began the count but did not finish it, and the next verse here says that Levi and Benjamin were left out. The two accounts may count different groups ("all Israel" here may take in more than the "Israel" of 2 Samuel), or the numbers may have been changed in copying; the text does not explain the difference.

decisions.choice: thousand: the ordinary number word
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 24:9 and in the census lists of Numbers (see the note at Numbers 1:21), the word is read as the number "thousand", though it can also name a military or clan unit, which would give smaller numbers.

decisions.choice: men who drew the sword: men fit for battle
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:9, which adds "men of strength". The phrase describes men who could be called up to fight (Judges 8:10; 20:2).

decisions.choice: men who could handle a sword (Balanced); men who could fight with a sword (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:9. Balanced and Readable keep the repeated phrase for Judah, as the Hebrew does.

alternatives: elfu mia nane; elfu mia tano
decisions.reason: Chronicles gives other totals from 2 Samuel 24:9; the Swahili writes Chronicles' figures in digits, as the English does.
Large round numbers in Korean figures with the unit 만, as 2 Samuel 24:9 in Korean writes "80만 명".

decisions.choice: um milhão e cem mil; quatrocentos e setenta mil (in words)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:9 in Portuguese ("o número do recenseamento", "empunhavam a espada" at Literal, "manejar a espada" at Balanced), with Chronicles' figures (m1) written in words at every level, as 2 Samuel 24:9 writes its round numbers in Portuguese, and the phrase repeated for Judah, as the Hebrew repeats it.

decisions.choice: 2 Samuel 24:9's Amharic with Chronicles' figures (1,100,000 and 470,000) and "ሰይፍ የሚመዝዙ" for both
decisions.reason: The figures and the repeated "who drew the sword" are Chronicles' own; 2 Samuel has 800,000 and 500,000.
These are the figures of this account (meaning m1), not those of 2 Samuel 24:9; they are written with Indian digit grouping, as 2 Samuel does.
The figures of this account differ from 2 Samuel 24:9 (m1); they are written as Samuel writes its census figures, with a thin no-break space.

decisions.choice: "百十万人", "四十七万人" in kanji numerals at every level, with no gender span (the English has none).
decisions.reason: Japanese numerals in running text, as the style guide.

source.text: וְלֵוִי֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן לֹ֥א פָקַ֖ד בְּתוֹכָ֑ם כִּֽי־נִתְעַ֥ב דְּבַר־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־יוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And Levi and Benjamin not he registered among them, for abhorrent was [the] word of the king to Joab.

en.L: But Levi and Benjamin he did not register among them, for the king's word was abhorrent to Joab.
en.B: But Levi and Benjamin he left out of the count, for Joab found the king's order hateful.
en.R: But Joab did not count the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he hated the king's order.

es.L: Pero a Leví y a Benjamín no los contó entre ellos, porque la palabra del rey era abominable para Joab.
es.B: Pero a Leví y a Benjamín los dejó fuera del censo, porque a Joab le resultaba odiosa la orden del rey.
es.R: Pero Joab no contó a las tribus de Leví y de Benjamín, porque odiaba la orden del rey.

fr.L: Mais Lévi et Benjamin, il ne les recensa pas parmi eux, car la parole du roi était une abomination pour Joab.
fr.B: Mais il laissa Lévi et Benjamin en dehors du recensement, car Joab avait l’ordre du roi en horreur.
fr.R: Mais Joab n’a pas compté les tribus de Lévi et de Benjamin, parce qu’il détestait l’ordre du roi.

sw.L: Lakini Lawi na Benyamini hakuwaandikisha miongoni mwao, kwa maana neno la mfalme lilikuwa chukizo kwa Yoabu.
sw.B: Lakini Lawi na Benyamini hakuwahesabu, kwa sababu Yoabu aliiona amri ya mfalme kuwa chukizo.
sw.R: Lakini Yoabu hakuyahesabu makabila ya Lawi na Benyamini, kwa sababu aliichukia amri ya mfalme.

vi.L: Nhưng ông không kiểm tra Lê-vi và Bên-gia-min trong số họ, vì lời vua là điều ghê tởm đối với Giô-áp.
vi.B: Nhưng ông không kiểm tra Lê-vi và Bên-gia-min, vì Giô-áp ghê tởm lệnh của vua.
vi.R: Nhưng Giô-áp không đếm các chi tộc Lê-vi và Bên-gia-min, vì ông ghét lệnh của vua.

ko.L: 그러나 레위와 베냐민은 그들 가운데 세지 않았다. 왕의 말이 요압에게 역겨웠기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 요압은 레위와 베냐민은 그 수에 넣지 않았다. 그는 왕의 명령을 몹시 싫어했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 요압은 레위 지파와 베냐민 지파는 세지 않았다. 그는 왕의 명령이 몹시 싫었기 때문이다.

pt.L: Mas Levi e Benjamim ele não recenseou entre eles, porque a palavra do rei era abominável para Joabe.
pt.B: Mas Levi e Benjamim ele deixou fora da contagem, porque Joabe achava detestável a ordem do rei.
pt.R: Mas Joabe não contou as tribos de Levi e de Benjamim, porque detestava a ordem do rei.

am.L: ሌዊንና ብንያምን ግን በመካከላቸው አልመዘገበም፤ የንጉሡ ቃል ለኢዮአብ አስጸያፊ ነበረና።
am.B: ሌዊንና ብንያምን ግን ከቆጠራው ውጭ አደረጋቸው፤ ኢዮአብ የንጉሡን ትእዛዝ ተጸይፎት ነበርና።
am.R: ኢዮአብ ግን የሌዊንና የብንያምን ነገዶች አልቆጠረም፤ የንጉሡን ትእዛዝ ጠልቶት ነበርና።

hi.L: पर लेवी और बिन्यामीन की उसने उनमें नाम-लिखाई नहीं की, क्योंकि राजा की बात योआब को घृणित लगी।
hi.B: पर लेवी और बिन्यामीन को उसने गिनती में शामिल नहीं किया, क्योंकि योआब को राजा का आदेश घृणित लगा।
hi.R: पर योआब ने लेवी और बिन्यामीन के गोत्रों की गिनती नहीं की, क्योंकि वह राजा के आदेश से घृणा करता था।

ru.L: А Левия и Вениамина он не переписал среди них, потому что слово царя было мерзко Иоаву.
ru.B: А Левия и Вениамина он не включил в перепись, потому что приказ царя был Иоаву ненавистен.
ru.R: Но Иоав не стал пересчитывать племена Левия и Вениамина, потому что ему был ненавистен приказ царя.

ja.L: しかしレビとベニヤミンを、彼はその中に登録しなかった。王の言葉がヨアブにとって忌まわしかったからである。
ja.B: しかし、レビとベニヤミンは数に入れなかった。ヨアブには王の命令が忌まわしく思われたからである。
ja.R: しかし、ヨアブは、レビの部族とベニヤミンの部族は数えませんでした。王の命令をひどく嫌っていたからです。

uk.L: А Левія й Веніямина він не переписав серед них, бо слово царя було огидне Йоавові.
uk.B: Але Левія й Веніямина він не включив до перепису, бо царський наказ був ненависний Йоавові.
uk.R: Але Йоав не перелічив племен Левія й Веніямина, бо ненавидів царський наказ.

decisions.choice: Levi and Benjamin not counted: a detail not in 2 Samuel 24
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24 says nothing of tribes left out. 1 Chronicles 27:24 says Joab began to count but did not finish. The law kept Levi out of the census of fighting men (Numbers 1:47-49), so leaving Levi out followed the law. The text does not say why Benjamin was left out, beyond Joab's dislike of the order.

decisions.choice: abhorrent: loathsome, detestable
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong one, used of what is disgusting or detestable. Joab, who had objected (verse 3), carried out the order but did not do all of it.

decisions.choice: Joab; the tribes of
decisions.reason: Readable names Joab as the one who did not count and calls Levi and Benjamin tribes.

decisions.choice: recenseou (L); abominável (L), detestável (B)
decisions.reason: "Recensear" is the census verb of 2 Samuel 24 at Literal; the strong verb of disgust (m2) is "abominável" at Literal and "detestável" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "አስጸያፊ" (abhorrent) for the Hebrew word of loathing, as Leviticus' "detestable"
decisions.reason: The word is a strong one; Balanced "ተጸይፎት" and Readable "ጠልቶት" keep its force in plainer verbs.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨רַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And was evil in [the] eyes of God concerning this thing, and he struck Israel.

en.L: And this thing was evil in the eyes of God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck Israel.
en.B: God was displeased with this thing, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck Israel.
en.R: God was not pleased with what David had done, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} punished Israel.

es.L: Y esta cosa fue mala a los ojos de Dios, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hirió a Israel.
es.B: A Dios le desagradó esto, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} castigó a Israel.
es.R: A Dios no le agradó lo que David había hecho, así que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} castigó a Israel.

fr.L: Et cette chose fut mauvaise aux yeux de Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappa Israël.
fr.B: Cette affaire déplut à Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappa Israël.
fr.R: Ce que David avait fait n’a pas plu à Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a puni Israël.

sw.L: Jambo hili likawa baya machoni pa Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawapiga Israeli.
sw.B: Mungu hakupendezwa na jambo hili, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawapiga Israeli.
sw.R: Mungu hakupendezwa na jambo ambalo Daudi alikuwa amefanya, kwa hiyo akawaadhibu Israeli.

vi.L: Việc này là điều ác trong mắt Đức Chúa Trời, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đánh phạt Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời không hài lòng về việc này, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đánh phạt Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời không vui về điều Đa-vít đã làm, nên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trừng phạt Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 이 일이 하나님의 눈에 악하였고, 그분께서 이스라엘을 치셨다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 이 일을 좋지 않게 여기셨고, 그분께서 이스라엘을 치셨다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 다윗이 한 일을 기뻐하지 않으셨다. 그래서 그분께서 이스라엘에 벌을 내리셨다.

pt.L: E esta coisa foi má aos olhos de Deus, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} feriu Israel.
pt.B: Deus se desagradou disso, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} feriu Israel.
pt.R: Deus não gostou do que Davi tinha feito, e por isso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} castigou Israel.

am.L: ይህም ነገር በእግዚአብሔር ዓይን ክፉ ሆነ፤ እስራኤልንም መታ።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር በዚህ ነገር ደስ አላለውም፤ እስራኤልንም መታ።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ዳዊት ባደረገው ነገር ደስ አላለውም፤ ስለዚህ እስራኤልን ቀጣ።

hi.L: और यह बात परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में बुरी थी, और उन्होंने इस्राएल को मारा।
hi.B: परमेश्वर इस बात से अप्रसन्न हुए, और उन्होंने इस्राएल को मारा।
hi.R: दाऊद ने जो किया था उससे परमेश्वर प्रसन्न नहीं थे, इसलिए उन्होंने इस्राएल को दंड दिया।

ru.L: И было злом в глазах Бога это дело, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} поразил Израиль.
ru.B: Это дело было злом в глазах Бога, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} поразил Израиль.
ru.R: Богу не понравилось то, что сделал Давид, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} наказал Израиль.

ja.L: そしてこのことは神の目に悪であった。そしてイスラエルを打たれた。
ja.B: 神はこのことを不快に思われ、イスラエルを打たれた。
ja.R: 神は、ダビデがしたことを喜ばれませんでした。それで、イスラエルを罰せられました。

uk.L: І було зле в Божих очах через цю справу, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} уразив Ізраїля.
uk.B: Богові не сподобалася ця справа, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} уразив Ізраїля.
uk.R: Богові не сподобалося те, що зробив Давид, тож {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} покарав Ізраїля.

decisions.choice: God was displeased and struck Israel: a verse not in 2 Samuel 24
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 24:10 it is David's own heart that "struck him" after the count, and he confesses before any word comes from God. Here God's displeasure comes first, and the same verb "struck" is used of what God does to Israel. David's confession follows in verse 8.

decisions.choice: he struck Israel: a summary of the judgment told in verses 14-15
alternatives: a first blow, before the plague, that led David to confess
decisions.reason: The plague itself is told after David's choice (verse 14). This short clause likely states in advance what the rest of the story tells in full. It could also describe a first blow, before the plague, that made David see his sin.

decisions.choice: was evil in the eyes of God: was displeasing to God
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" means in someone's judgment. The census was wrong in God's sight.

decisions.choice: was displeased with (Balanced); was not pleased with what David had done; punished (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the idiom in plain words. Readable says what "this thing" was and says "punished" for "struck".

decisions.choice: feriu (L, B); castigou (R)
decisions.reason: "Feriu" keeps the verb that 2 Samuel 24:10 in Portuguese uses for David's heart striking him (m1); Readable says "castigou", as the English says "punished".

decisions.choice: Elohim ("the God") is "እግዚአብሔር" with no divine_name span, here and in verses 8, 15, 17 and 30
decisions.reason: The text is plainly about the one God and the divine name does not stand beside the word, so it takes the name Ethiopian readers use for God; only YHWH is under the divine_name setting.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span; honorific "उन्होंने" for God
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the Hindi has no deity_pronoun spans (style guide, section 7); respect for God is carried by the honorific third person in the narrative and by "तू" in prayer. This holds wherever the English has such a span in this chapter.

decisions.choice: "было злом в глазах Бога" (Literal, Balanced); "не понравилось" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words of the regnal verdict in the history note.

decisions.choice: No pronoun for God: the respect form "打たれた" (L, B), "罰せられました" (R) shows the subject.
decisions.reason: The style guide: never 彼 for God; Japanese leaves the pronoun out.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים חָטָ֣אתִֽי מְאֹ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְעַתָּ֗ה הַֽעֲבֶר־נָא֙ אֶת־עֲו֣וֹן עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֥י נִסְכַּ֖לְתִּי מְאֹֽד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said David to God, I have sinned greatly that I have done this thing; and now, take away, please, [the] iniquity of your servant, for I have acted foolishly exceedingly.

en.L: And David said to God, "I have sinned greatly in that I have done this thing. And now, please take away the iniquity of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
en.B: Then David said to God, "I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now please take away {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant's guilt, for I have acted very foolishly."
en.R: Then David said to God, "I have done a very sinful thing. Now please take away my guilt. I have been very foolish."

es.L: Y dijo David a Dios: «He pecado gravemente al hacer esto. Y ahora, te ruego que quites la iniquidad de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo, porque he actuado muy neciamente».
es.B: Entonces David le dijo a Dios: «He pecado gravemente al hacer esto. Ahora te ruego que quites la culpa de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo, porque he actuado con mucha necedad».
es.R: Entonces David le dijo a Dios: «He hecho algo muy malo. Ahora, por favor, quítame la culpa. He sido muy necio».

fr.L: Et David dit à Dieu : « J’ai gravement péché en ce que j’ai fait cette chose. Et maintenant, enlève, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, la faute de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, car j’ai agi très follement. »
fr.B: Alors David dit à Dieu : « J’ai gravement péché en agissant ainsi. Maintenant, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, efface la faute de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, car j’ai agi comme un insensé. »
fr.R: Alors David a dit à Dieu : « J’ai commis un grand péché. Maintenant, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, enlève ma faute. J’ai été très bête. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Mungu, "Nimetenda dhambi kubwa kwa kuwa nimefanya jambo hili. Na sasa, tafadhali uondoe uovu wa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, kwa maana nimetenda kwa upumbavu sana."
sw.B: Kisha Daudi akamwambia Mungu, "Nimetenda dhambi kubwa kwa kufanya hivi. Sasa tafadhali uondoe hatia ya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, kwa maana nimetenda kwa upumbavu sana."
sw.R: Kisha Daudi akamwambia Mungu, "Nimetenda dhambi kubwa sana. Sasa tafadhali niondolee hatia yangu. Nimekuwa mpumbavu sana."

vi.L: Đa-vít thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: "Con đã phạm tội nặng vì đã làm việc này. Bây giờ, xin cất bỏ tội lỗi của đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì con đã hành động rất dại dột."
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đa-vít thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: "Con đã phạm tội nặng khi làm việc này. Bây giờ xin tha tội cho đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì con đã hành động rất dại dột."
vi.R: Bấy giờ Đa-vít thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: "Con đã làm một việc rất tội lỗi. Bây giờ xin tha tội cho con. Con đã quá dại dột."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 하나님께 말씀드렸다. "제가 이 일을 하여 큰 죄를 지었습니다. 그러니 이제 부디 주님의 종의 죄악을 없애 주십시오. 제가 너무나 어리석은 짓을 했습니다."
ko.B: 그러자 다윗이 하나님께 아뢰었다. "제가 이 일로 큰 죄를 지었습니다. 이제 주님의 종의 죄를 없애 주십시오. 제가 너무나 어리석은 짓을 했습니다."
ko.R: 그러자 다윗이 하나님께 아뢰었다. "제가 아주 큰 죄를 지었습니다. 이제 제 죄를 없애 주십시오. 제가 너무 어리석었습니다."

pt.L: E Davi disse a Deus: "Pequei muito, porque fiz esta coisa. E agora tira, por favor, a iniquidade do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo, pois agi muito insensatamente."
pt.B: Então Davi disse a Deus: "Pequei gravemente ao fazer isso. Agora, por favor, tira a culpa do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo, pois agi como um grande insensato."
pt.R: Então Davi disse a Deus: "Fiz uma coisa muito errada. Agora, por favor, tira a minha culpa. Fui muito tolo."

am.L: ዳዊትም ለእግዚአብሔር እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህን ነገር በማድረጌ እጅግ ኃጢአት ሠርቻለሁ። አሁንም እባክህ የባሪያህን በደል አስወግድ፤ እጅግ ሞኝነት አድርጌአለሁና።»
am.B: ከዚያም ዳዊት ለእግዚአብሔር እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህን በማድረጌ እጅግ ኃጢአት ሠርቻለሁ። አሁንም እባክህ የአገልጋይህን በደል አስወግድ፤ እጅግ የሞኝነት ሥራ ሠርቻለሁና።»
am.R: ከዚያም ዳዊት ለእግዚአብሔር እንዲህ አለ፦ «እጅግ ክፉ ኃጢአት ሠርቻለሁ። አሁንም እባክህ በደሌን አስወግድልኝ። እጅግ ሞኝ ሆኛለሁ።»

hi.L: और दाऊद ने परमेश्वर से कहा, "मैंने बड़ा पाप किया है कि यह काम किया है। और अब, कृपया अपने दास का अधर्म दूर कर, क्योंकि मैंने बड़ी मूर्खता की है।"
hi.B: तब दाऊद ने परमेश्वर से कहा, "यह करके मैंने बड़ा पाप किया है। अब कृपया अपने दास का दोष दूर कर, क्योंकि मैंने बड़ी मूर्खता की है।"
hi.R: तब दाऊद ने परमेश्वर से कहा, "मैंने बहुत बड़ा पाप किया है। अब कृपया मेरा दोष दूर कर। मैंने बड़ी मूर्खता की है।"

ru.L: И сказал Давид Богу: «Я тяжко согрешил тем, что сделал это дело. А теперь сними, прошу, беззаконие {{deity_pronoun:твоего|Твоего}} раба, потому что я поступил очень безрассудно.»
ru.B: Тогда Давид сказал Богу: «Я тяжко согрешил, сделав это. А теперь, прошу, сними вину с {{deity_pronoun:твоего|Твоего}} раба, потому что я поступил очень глупо.»
ru.R: Тогда Давид сказал Богу: «Я совершил тяжкий грех. А теперь, прошу, сними с меня вину. Я поступил очень глупо.»

ja.L: そしてダビデは神に言った。「わたしは、このことを行って、大きな罪を犯しました。そして今、どうか、あなたのしもべの咎を取り去ってください。わたしは非常に愚かなことをしました。」
ja.B: そこでダビデは神に言った。「わたしは、このようなことをして、大きな罪を犯しました。今、どうか、しもべの咎を取り除いてください。わたしは本当に愚かなことをいたしました。」
ja.R: そこでダビデは神に言いました。「わたしは、とても悪いことをしてしまいました。どうか、わたしの罪を取り除いてください。わたしは本当に愚かでした。」

uk.L: І сказав Давид Богові: «Я тяжко згрішив тим, що зробив цю справу. А тепер, прошу, зніми провину з {{deity_pronoun:твого|Твого}} раба, бо я вчинив дуже нерозумно.»
uk.B: Тоді Давид сказав Богові: «Я тяжко згрішив, зробивши це. Тепер, прошу, зніми провину з {{deity_pronoun:твого|Твого}} раба, бо я вчинив дуже нерозумно.»
uk.R: Тоді Давид сказав Богові: «Я вчинив дуже великий гріх. Тепер, прошу, зніми з мене провину. Я вчинив дуже нерозумно.»

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 24:10
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:10 opens with "David's heart struck him after he had counted the people" and has David speak to "Yahweh", calling on him by name a second time ("and now, Yahweh, take away ..."). Here David speaks to "God", with no name in the plea, and says "in that I have done this thing" for "in what I have done". The rest is the same.

decisions.choice: take away the iniquity: remove the guilt and its punishment
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:10. The word for iniquity covers both the wrong and the guilt it brings.

decisions.choice: your servant: a humble way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:10: speaking to a superior, a person called himself "your servant".

decisions.choice: your servant (Literal, Balanced); my (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:10: Literal and Balanced keep the polite form; Readable says "my guilt", which is what it means.

decisions.choice: David prays in 합쇼체, calling himself "주님의 종" (L, B) and "제" (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 24:10 in Korean.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 24:10, to "Deus", without the vocative "SENHOR"
decisions.reason: David's prayer keeps 2 Samuel 24:10 in Portuguese at every level ("tira", "o teu servo", "insensatamente" / "insensato" / "tolo"; "tu" to God), but he speaks to "Deus" and there is no "SENHOR" after "agora", as Chronicles has it (m1); Literal says "porque fiz esta coisa" for Chronicles' added clause.

decisions.choice: David prays with "አንተ" and calls himself "ባሪያህ" (L), "አገልጋይህ" (B), as in 2 Samuel 24:10
decisions.reason: The prayer keeps 2 Samuel 24:10's Amharic; Chronicles has "God" for the divine name, adds "this thing" and has no second address to Yahweh, and the Amharic follows.

decisions.choice: the Russian of 2 Samuel 24:10, with "Богу"
decisions.reason: Chronicles has David speak to God, without Samuel's "his heart struck him" and its "LORD" in the prayer (m1).

decisions.choice: David to God in です・ます; "あなたのしもべ" (L), "しもべ" (B), "わたし" (R), as 2 Samuel 24:10.
decisions.reason: Humble self-reference as the English levels.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 24:11
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:11 begins "And David rose in the morning" and says that "the word of Yahweh came to Gad the prophet, David's seer". Here Yahweh simply "spoke" to Gad, with no time given and no title "the prophet". The word for "seer" is the same in both.

decisions.choice: Gad, David's seer: a prophet who served at David's court
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:11. Gad was with David from his years as a fugitive (1 Samuel 22:5), and 1 Chronicles 29:29 names him among those who recorded David's history. "Seer" is an older title for a prophet, one to whom God shows things.

decisions.choice: a prophet who brought David messages from God; The LORD said to Gad
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:11: Readable explains "seer" the first time it appears in this chapter and names the speaker of the next verse.

decisions.choice: a colon in place of "saying"
decisions.reason: Balanced introduces the message with a colon, since it begins in the next verse.

decisions.choice: "nhà tiên tri Gát"
decisions.reason: As the Vietnamese Samuel, the prophet Gad always carries his title, because "Gát" is also the city of Gath and the tribe of Gad.

decisions.choice: "선견자", explained at Readable
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's word for the seer; Readable explains it the first time it appears, as 2 Samuel 24:11 in Korean does.

decisions.choice: Gade, o vidente de Davi
decisions.reason: "Gade" and "o vidente" as 2 Samuel 24:11 in Portuguese, with Readable's explanation from there; Chronicles has no morning and no "o profeta" (m1), so neither does the Portuguese.

decisions.choice: "ባለ ራእይ" (seer), as in 2 Samuel 24:11
decisions.reason: Chronicles has Yahweh speak to Gad directly, without the morning and "the prophet"; the title keeps the Amharic of the parallel.

decisions.choice: "दाऊद के दर्शी गाद"
decisions.reason: Seer is "दर्शी", as 2 Samuel 24:11 and the history-books note; Readable explains it there and here, as the English does. Gad says "तुम" to David, as in 2 Samuel 24, and the LORD's words through him use "तुम".

decisions.choice: chozeh "先見者" at every level, as 2 Samuel 24:11.
decisions.reason: The same title in the parallel.

records.literal_gloss: Go and speak to David, saying, Thus says Yahweh: Three [things] I [am] holding out over you; choose for yourself one of them, and I will do [it] to you.

en.L: "Go and speak to David, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Three [things] I am holding out to you. Choose for yourself one of them, and I will do [it] to you.'"
en.B: "Go and tell David, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am offering you three things. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
en.R: "Go and tell David, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am giving you three choices. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"

es.L: «Ve y habla a David, diciendo: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Tres [cosas] te propongo. Escoge para ti una de ellas, y te la haré”».
es.B: «Ve y dile a David: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Te ofrezco tres cosas. Escoge una de ellas, y eso te haré”».
es.R: «Ve y dile a David: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Te doy tres opciones. Escoge una de ellas, y eso te haré”».

fr.L: « Va et parle à David, en disant : “Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je te présente trois [choses]. Choisis-toi l’une d’elles, et je te la ferai.” »
fr.B: « Va dire à David : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je te propose trois choses. Choisis-en une, et c’est celle-là que je t’infligerai.” »
fr.R: « Va dire à David : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je te donne trois choix. Choisis-en un, et c’est ce que je te ferai.” »

sw.L: "Nenda useme na Daudi, kusema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Mambo matatu ninakunyooshea. Ujichagulie moja wapo, nami nitakutendea [hilo].'"
sw.B: "Nenda ukamwambie Daudi, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ninakupa mambo matatu. Chagua moja wapo, nami nitakutendea hilo.'"

vi.L: "Hãy đi nói với Đa-vít rằng: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Ta đưa ra cho ngươi ba [điều]. Hãy chọn cho mình một trong ba điều ấy, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm [điều đó] cho ngươi.'"
vi.B: "Hãy đi nói với Đa-vít: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Ta đưa ra cho con ba điều. Hãy chọn một trong ba, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm điều đó cho con.'"
vi.R: "Hãy đi nói với Đa-vít: 'Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Ta cho con ba điều để chọn. Hãy chọn một, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm điều đó cho con.'"

ko.L: "가서 다윗에게 말하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 내가 너에게 세 가지를 내놓는다. 너는 그 가운데 하나를 골라라. 내가 그것을 너에게 행하겠다.'"
ko.B: "가서 다윗에게 전하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 네 앞에 세 가지를 내놓으니, 그 가운데 하나를 골라라. 내가 그것을 너에게 내리겠다.'"
ko.R: "가서 다윗에게 전하여라. '이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이다. 내가 너에게 세 가지 가운데 하나를 고르게 하겠다. 하나를 골라라. 그러면 내가 그것을 너에게 내리겠다.'"

pt.L: "Vai e fala a Davi, dizendo: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Três [coisas] eu estendo diante de ti. Escolhe para ti uma delas, e eu a farei contigo.'"
pt.B: "Vai dizer a Davi: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} diz isto: Eu te ofereço três coisas. Escolhe uma delas, e eu a farei contigo.'"
pt.R: "Vai falar com Davi: 'Isto é o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Eu te dou três escolhas. Escolhe uma delas, e eu a farei contigo.'"

ru.L: «Пойди и скажи Давиду, говоря: “Так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}: Три [вещи] {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} протягиваю тебе. Выбери себе одну из них, и {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сделаю [её] тебе.”»

decisions.choice: holding out: a different verb from 2 Samuel 24:12
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:12 has a verb meaning "lay on": three burdens laid on David. Here the verb means to stretch out or hold out, so the three are held out for David to choose from. This verse also adds "saying" before the message. Otherwise the words are the same.

decisions.choice: choose one of them: the punishment is certain, its form is left to David
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:12. Yahweh does not let the sin pass, but he lets David choose how the punishment will come.

decisions.choice: double quotes for Yahweh's words to Gad, single quotes for the message to David
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 24:12: Gad is to pass on Yahweh's words, so they stand as a quotation inside Yahweh's own speech.

decisions.choice: offering you three things (Balanced); giving you three choices (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense of "holding out three over you" in natural English.

decisions.choice: BWANA asema hivi (L); Hivi ndivyo BWANA asemavyo (B); Hili ndilo BWANA analosema (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula takes one wording per level through this block, as in 1 Chronicles 17:4; 2 Samuel 24:12 used other orders, which a reviewer may bring into line.

decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 24:12 in Portuguese, with the LORD speaking to Gad and to David with "tu", changed only for Chronicles' verb "hold out" (m1): "estendo diante de ti" at Literal and "te ofereço" at Balanced, where 2 Samuel has "ponho sobre ti" / "ponho diante de ti".

decisions.choice: Gad gives the choices as Yahweh's own words: a difference from 2 Samuel 24:13
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 24:13 Gad "told him, and said to him", and put the three choices to David as questions in his own words. Here he opens with "Thus says Yahweh" and passes on the offer as Yahweh's speech, as Yahweh told him to (verse 10).

decisions.choice: take for yourself: accept one, take your pick
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive or accept. With "for yourself" it invites David to take whichever of the three he will. It is the same offer as "choose for yourself" in verse 10.

decisions.choice: double quotes for Gad's speech, single quotes for Yahweh's words; neither closed here
decisions.reason: Gad's speech runs into verse 12. The words he passes on from Yahweh close in verse 12 before his own closing question, and his speech closes at the end of that verse.

decisions.choice: quotation marks « “ left open
decisions.reason: Gad's speech and the LORD's words inside it run on into verse 12, so neither mark is closed here, as in the English.

decisions.choice: Gad speaks to the king in 합쇼체 ("말씀하십니다"); the LORD's words inside are in 해라체
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 24:12-13 in Korean: the prophet uses court courtesy, and God speaks in the plain style.

decisions.choice: tu inside the LORD's words; Toma para ti (L), Escolhe (B, R)
decisions.reason: Gad passes on the LORD's own words (m1), so inside the single quotes the LORD speaks to David with "tu", as in verse 10; Gad's own question at the end of verse 12 uses "você", as Gad speaks to the king in 2 Samuel 24:13 in Portuguese. Literal keeps "toma para ti" (m2); Balanced and Readable say "escolhe".

decisions.reason: Gad's speech runs on into verse 12.

source.text: אִם־שָׁל֨וֹשׁ שָׁנִ֜ים רָעָ֗ב וְאִם־שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה חֳדָשִׁ֜ים נִסְפֶּ֥ה מִפְּנֵי־צָרֶיךָ֮ וְחֶ֣רֶב אוֹיְבֶ֣ךָ׀לְמַשֶּׂגֶת֒ וְאִם־שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָ֠מִים חֶ֣רֶב יְהוָ֤ה וְדֶ֨בֶר֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה מַשְׁחִ֖ית בְּכָל־גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֣ה רְאֵ֔ה מָֽה־אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: whether three years [of] famine, or three months [of] being swept away before your foes, and [the] sword of your enemies to overtake, or three days [of the] sword of Yahweh and pestilence in the land, and [the] angel of Yahweh destroying in all [the] territory of Israel. And now consider what I shall return [to] the one sending me [as a] word.

en.L: either three years of famine, or three months of being swept away before your foes while the sword of your enemies overtakes [you], or three days of the sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, pestilence in the land, with the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroying throughout all the territory of Israel.' And now consider what word I shall return to the one who sent me."
en.B: three years of famine; or three months of being swept away by your foes, with the sword of your enemies catching up with you; or three days of the sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a plague in the land, with the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bringing destruction throughout all the territory of Israel.' Now decide what answer I should take back to the one who sent me."
en.R: three years of famine; or three months of being swept away by your enemies, as their swords catch up with you; or three days when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own sword. That would be a deadly plague in the land, with the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bringing death all through Israel.' Think about it and decide. Then tell me what answer I should give to the one who sent me."

es.L: o tres años de hambre, o tres meses de ser destruido delante de tus adversarios mientras la espada de tus enemigos te alcanza, o tres días de la espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, peste en la tierra, con el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} destruyendo por todo el territorio de Israel”. Y ahora considera qué palabra he de llevar al que me envió».
es.B: tres años de hambre; o tres meses de ser arrasado por tus adversarios, mientras la espada de tus enemigos te alcanza; o tres días de la espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, una peste en la tierra, con el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} trayendo destrucción por todo el territorio de Israel”. Ahora decide qué respuesta debo llevarle al que me envió».
es.R: tres años de hambre; o tres meses de ser arrasado por tus enemigos, mientras sus espadas te alcanzan; o tres días en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} herirá con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia espada. Eso sería una peste mortal en la tierra, y el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} traería muerte por todo Israel”. Piénsalo y decide. Luego dime qué respuesta le debo dar al que me envió».

fr.L: ou trois ans de famine, ou trois mois d’être balayé devant tes adversaires, tandis que l’épée de tes ennemis [t’]atteindra, ou trois jours de l’épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, la peste dans le pays, avec l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui détruira dans tout le territoire d’Israël.” Et maintenant, vois quelle parole je dois rapporter à celui qui m’a envoyé. »
fr.B: trois années de famine ; ou trois mois où tu seras balayé par tes adversaires, tandis que l’épée de tes ennemis te rattrapera ; ou trois jours de l’épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, la peste dans le pays, avec l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui portera la destruction dans tout le territoire d’Israël.” Décide maintenant quelle réponse je dois rapporter à celui qui m’a envoyé. »
fr.R: trois années de famine ; ou trois mois pendant lesquels tes ennemis te balaieront et où leurs épées te rattraperont ; ou trois jours où {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} frappera avec {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre épée. Ce sera une peste mortelle dans le pays, et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} apportera la mort dans tout Israël.” Réfléchis et décide-toi. Ensuite, dis-moi quelle réponse je dois donner à celui qui m’a envoyé. »

sw.L: ama miaka mitatu ya njaa, au miezi mitatu ya kufagiliwa mbele ya watesi wako na upanga wa adui zako ukikupata, au siku tatu za upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tauni katika nchi, na malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akiangamiza katika eneo lote la Israeli.' Na sasa fikiri ni neno gani nimrudishie yule aliyenituma."
sw.B: miaka mitatu ya njaa; au miezi mitatu ya kufagiliwa na watesi wako, upanga wa adui zako ukikufikia; au siku tatu za upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yaani tauni katika nchi, malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akileta maangamizi katika eneo lote la Israeli.' Sasa amua ni jibu gani nimpelekee yule aliyenituma."
sw.R: miaka mitatu ya njaa; au miezi mitatu ya kufagiliwa na adui zako, panga zao zikikufikia; au siku tatu ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atapiga kwa upanga wake mwenyewe. Hiyo itakuwa tauni ya kuua katika nchi, malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akileta vifo katika Israeli yote.' Fikiri uamue. Kisha uniambie jibu nitakalompa yule aliyenituma."

vi.L: hoặc ba năm đói kém, hoặc ba tháng bị quét sạch trước mặt kẻ thù trong khi gươm của kẻ thù đuổi kịp [ngươi], hoặc ba ngày gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, là dịch bệnh trong xứ, với thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hủy diệt khắp cả lãnh thổ Y-sơ-ra-ên.' Bây giờ xin vua hãy xem tôi phải đem lời nào về trả lời Đấng đã sai tôi."
vi.B: ba năm đói kém; hoặc ba tháng bị kẻ thù quét sạch, gươm của kẻ thù đuổi kịp con; hoặc ba ngày gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, là dịch lệ trong xứ, với thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hủy diệt khắp cả lãnh thổ Y-sơ-ra-ên.' Bây giờ xin bệ hạ quyết định tôi phải đem câu trả lời nào về cho Đấng đã sai tôi."
vi.R: ba năm đói kém; hoặc ba tháng bị kẻ thù quét sạch, khi gươm của chúng đuổi kịp con; hoặc ba ngày {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} dùng chính gươm của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà đánh. Đó sẽ là một bệnh dịch chết người trong xứ, với thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đem sự chết đến khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên.' Xin đức vua suy nghĩ và quyết định. Rồi cho tôi biết tôi phải trả lời thế nào với Đấng đã sai tôi."

ko.L: 세 해 동안의 기근이든지, 아니면 네 적들 앞에서 석 달 동안 쓸려 가고 네 원수들의 칼이 [너를] 따라잡는 것이든지, 아니면 사흘 동안 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 칼, 곧 그 땅에 전염병이 [돌고] {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 이스라엘 온 지역을 멸하는 것이든지 하여라.' 이제 저를 보내신 분께 제가 무슨 대답을 가지고 돌아가야 할지 잘 생각해 보십시오."
